follow-up time: During pregnancy and for 6 weeks postpartum
exposure: Source of infection (genital tract, urinary tract, other)
Gestational age at sepsis onset (antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum)
cohort: 150,043 pregnant women attending two tertiary referral maternity hospitals in Dublin, Ireland, between 2005 and 2012.
finding: Maternal sepsis was associated with a rate of 1.81 per 1000 pregnant women, predominantly caused by Escherichia coli and Group B Streptococcus, and was linked to preterm birth, high perinatal mortality, and increased risk in nulliparous women.
